### Promptless documentation updates

- [Update Theme sandbox restrictions for Twig collection filters](https://app.gopromptless.ai/suggestions/77050cfe-f4e2-4088-9f3c-ad82488bfcb9) updates the "Template sandbox restrictions" section of the 7.2 developer docs: the sandbox now blocks only risky functions, and Theme templates can use `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `sort` and `find` with arrow-function callbacks. [Docs PR](https://github.com/mautic/developer-documentation-new/pull/714)
Can you please provide steps to test? What filter wasn't working?

Thanks for asking. The issue is the Mautic theme sandbox denylist, not a missing Twig filter.

### Reproduction

1. Use a clean Mautic 7.2.1 installation.
2. Create a theme under `themes/` with a `page.html.twig` template.
3. Add a normal collection-filter expression to the template:

```twig
{% block content %}
    {{ [3, 1, 2]|sort|join }}
{% endblock %}
```

4. Create a page using that theme and open its preview.

On the current 7.2.1 code, the sandbox policy rejects `sort` before Twig can execute it, because Mautic's `ThemeSandboxPolicy` contains a denylist for collection filters. The same applies to legitimate uses of `map`, `filter` and `reduce`.

### What the PR changes

The PR removes Mautic's redundant filter denylist. Twig's own sandbox still validates callable arguments, so ordinary collection-filter usage is allowed while PHP function-name callbacks remain blocked.

I tested the patched policy in a clean 7.2.1 Composer sandbox with these cases:

```twig
{{ [3, 1, 2]|sort|join }}
```

Result:

```
123
```

The RCE-style callback cases were also tested:

```twig
{{ ["id", 0]|sort("system")|join }}
{{ ["id", 0]|find("system") }}
```

Both are rejected by Twig's sandbox with a runtime security error. The existing `map`, `filter` and `reduce` callback regression tests remain in place, and the PR adds equivalent coverage for `sort` and `find`.

So the expected verification is:

- normal `sort`/collection-filter expressions render successfully;
- callbacks supplied as PHP function-name strings are rejected;
- no command output or file content is exposed.

The complete CI matrix for this PR is green, including PHPUnit, e2e, PHPStan, CS Fixer, Twig Lint and SonarCloud.

### Promptless documentation updates

- [Update ClassMetadataBuilder association-builder return types for Doctrine ORM 3](https://app.gopromptless.ai/suggestions/f4636ec1-6b9a-4bcc-a7ed-c9ef3578446c) corrects the documented return types for `ClassMetadataBuilder::createManyToMany()` and `createOneToMany()` to Doctrine's own builder classes, since this PR removes Mautic's decorator classes. [Docs PR](https://github.com/mautic/developer-documentation-new/pull/667)

> Also there is a lot of retyping to string which I don't understand.

DBAL 3 took mixed values. DBAL 4 changed `ExpressionBuilder` to accept only strings, so anything passed has to be a string now.

For example, see `ExpressionBuilder::eq()`

DBAL 3: https://github.com/doctrine/dbal/blob/77eb61f529ee8a99152afdc955ff606f7ce21474/src/Query/Expression/ExpressionBuilder.php#L115-L133
DBAL 4: https://github.com/doctrine/dbal/blob/205fdf552ffafe33c1d12a41a2d6c7217666c32c/src/Query/Expression/ExpressionBuilder.php#L66-L82

On `(string) ((int) $campaignId)` specifically:
```diff
-$q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (int) $campaignId),
+$q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (string) ((int) $campaignId)),
```

These values are embedded as SQL literals rather than bound parameters, so the `(int)` is the existing guard against injection, only the `(string)` is required by DBAL 4. I checked the cases where the parameter is already typed, they are all `?int` with no null guard, so dropping the `(int)` would turn null into `''` and emit `campaign_id = `.

You were right that much of it was noise, though 38 of the casts were on literals (`(string) (0)`, `(string) (1)`, `(string) (true)`, `(string) (200)`). Those are now plain `'0'`, `'1'`, `'200'`.

Binding these as parameters instead of embedding them would remove the remaining casts entirely, but that is a real refactor and it would be better to do it separately than in this PR.

For example
```diff
-    public function getCountsForPendingContacts($campaignId, array $pendingEvents, ContactLimiter $limiter): CountResult
+    public function getCountsForPendingContacts(int $campaignId, array $pendingEvents, ContactLimiter $limiter): CountResult
-                    $q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (string) ((int) $campaignId)),
+                    $q->expr()->eq('cl.campaign_id', (string) $campaignId),
```

Update on the CI failure I flagged above: it isn't caused by this documentation change.

The failing step is the Sphinx link check (`make checklinks`), which failed on a single external link — `https://opencollective.com/mautic` returning `403 Forbidden` to the checker. That link lives in `docs/index.rst` (via `docs/links/mautic_open_collective.py`), not in the `docs/rest_api/companies.rst` page this PR edits, and the identical content on the non-8.0 sibling PR passed the same check — so the 403 is a flaky/bot-blocked external site rather than a docs defect here. Re-running the link-check job (or allowlisting `opencollective.com` in the linkcheck config if it keeps returning 403) should clear it.

While investigating, I did spot and fix three 'Title underline too short' RST warnings that this PR's own added section had introduced; that fix is pushed here, and Vale and rstcheck are now clean.

Thanks @adiati98 — all three suggestions applied in the latest commit, and I dug into why the links weren't rendering.

- **Features list** → bare targets: `:ref:`html/email.html.twig``, `:ref:`html/form.html.twig``, `:ref:`html/page.html.twig``
- **Corresponding-file paragraph** → `:ref:`Twig files``
- **Form style-only Themes note** → `:doc:`/themes/forms``

**Root cause of the broken links:** `docs/conf.py` sets `autosectionlabel_prefix_document = True`, which generates document-prefixed labels (including the literal backticks in headings like `` ``html/email.html.twig`` ``). That's why neither the previous prefixed form nor a plain bare `:ref:` resolved. To make the bare-target syntax you requested actually work, I added explicit reference labels at the four target headings:

```
.. _Twig files:
.. _html/email.html.twig:
.. _html/page.html.twig:
.. _html/form.html.twig:
```

**Verification:** A full Sphinx build confirms all four cross-references now render as real internal links and `:doc:`/themes/forms`` resolves to "Customizing Forms". No new undefined-label or duplicate-label warnings. Vale passes on the edited lines (which sit inside the existing `.. vale off`/`.. vale on` block).

Heads-up: the bare `:ref:` format works only because of those added heading labels — without them, bare targets would still fail under this repo's `autosectionlabel_prefix_document` setting.

The documentation is mostly aligned with the feature change, but one wording detail should be tightened after the latest review feedback on #16257: the relaxed import requirement now applies only to style-only Form Themes, meaning Themes that declare only the `form` feature and include a Form style override file.

Mixed-feature Themes, for example `features: ["form", "email"]`, should still require the normal template files for the declared features.

Could we update the note to say something like "A Theme that declares only the `form` feature..." and mention that the exception does not apply when the Theme also declares other features such as `email` or `page`?

Once that wording is updated, the docs will match the current implementation.

The note now states that the exception applies only when a Theme declares **only** the `form` feature (with a Form style override file), so it doesn't require `html/form.html.twig` or `html/message.html.twig`. It also clarifies that the exception does **not** apply to mixed-feature Themes (for example `features: ["form", "email"]` or those that also declare `page`), which still require the normal template files for each declared feature. Verified against the `['form'] === $features` check in mautic/mautic#16257.

## Pull request overview This PR adds Dynamic Web Content–style contact filters to Focus items so that eligible published Focus items can be automatically injected on tracked visits via `mtc.js`, without requiring manual embeds or campaigns. **Changes:** - Adds a nullable `filters` column to `focus` (via migration) and exposes it via serializer groups for Focus API read/write. - Extends the Focus edit UI with a new Filters tab using the existing DWC filters entry type/theme and shared filter JS initialization. - Implements automatic delivery: `mtc.js` conditionally calls a new public `/focus/check` endpoint which returns matching Focus item JS URLs for the tracked contact, with functional tests covering key scenarios. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 17 out of 17 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

Please take a look at this:

Bulk contact export ignores `viewsamerole` (real gap)
Updates the `contact index` to respect `viewsamerole`, but `batchExportAction` still uses the old `ismine` filter whenever `viewother` is missing.

- `Contact list:` `owner_id IN (all users with the same role)`
- `Bulk export:` `owner_id = current user only`

A user can see contacts owned by teammates in the same role, but export fewer contacts than the list shows.

Related gaps (same pattern, not fixed in PR)
- `SearchSubscriber::onGlobalSearchForContacts()` — contact global search still uses `ismine` only

TY!

One architectural concern worth discussing is that this approach uses roles for two different concepts: the user’s access level and the user’s team/group boundary.

For example, if Italy marketers and Italy managers need different permissions, they cannot both simply use a `Italy` role. The installation may need roles like `Germany Marketer`, `Germany Manager`, `Italy Marketer`, `Italy Manager`, etc.

That can become harder to manage as the number of countries, offices, brands, or teams grows. It also makes cases like users belonging to multiple teams or managers needing cross-team access more difficult to model - this approach is not possible with permissions.

A separate team/group concept could keep these concerns apart: roles define what a user can do, while teams/groups define which records they can access.

Not saying this blocks the PR, but it feels worth discussing so we are clear whether same-role permissions are the right direction here.

I was quite excited about the [proposal](https://community.mautic.org/processes/roadmap/f/4/proposals/200) as it was suggesting to bend Postgres with polyfills to support Mautic rather than bending Mautic to support Postgres. However, in this PR I can see major Mautic refactoring. Lots of ifs where one query is used for MySql and MariaDB and completely different query is used for Postgres. When you look at the size of this PR it's clear how massive change it is. It'll take weeks just to review this. I'm pretty sure there are tens of bugs hidden in this PR. So we'll need good user base that require Mautic running on Postgres that will help us review and test this PR. Because if it is still just 1% then such a massive change that makes the code even harder to maintain isn't worth it. This is why we've decided to drop support for Posgres in the first place.

I've considered a better database abstraction layer for Mautic for some time. Inserting another abstraction layer for all data-driven interactions is very appealing. Such a mechanism would allow us to use different backend data sources  depending on what's being requested. Have some documents in MongoDB? Go get them through the data layer Mongo datasource. Need to operate on your campaigns from Salesforce? Get them through the data layer's Salesforce datasource. This would prevent us from having to manage the seemingly neverending data sync issues that come hand-in-hand with our current integrations. 

There's plenty of architectural benefits of this approach. By managing the data layer in this way, we could intercept and act on any request for data, modifying or otherwise combining various data sources into a normalized structure. We could take a request like `$this->datalayer->contacts->all()` and pull in local db contacts, remote contacts from an API response, and query the filesystem of an old ERP. We could more easily implement an [event sourcing](https://eventsauce.io/) approach which comes with all sorts of benefits on its own (data rollbacks, replays, insight into what happened for audit purposes). 

That said, such a system could be rather impractical both to implement and in real world usage without major changes that go beyond the scope of what even this PR is trying to accomplish. I'm not opposed to supporting pgsql, but I would like to see it implemented in a particular way if we really want it. I'm open to discussion.

Thanks for the detailed reviews, @escopecz @shinde-rahul @dongilbert. You're right to call out the scattered DB-specific logic and the growth in scope.

The original plan was a small, contained change like the POC: mostly platform tweaks, quoting fixes, and minimal adjustments to keep everything working on both MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL without breaking existing installs. Doctrine 2.x limits cleaner abstraction options, so some conditionals and duplicated query parts crept in as we hit real edge cases in tests and production data. Things like LIKE vs ILIKE (with LOWER), REGEXP differences, date formatting (DATE_FORMAT vs TO_CHAR), GROUP BY strictness, and upsert behavior all needed handling. The PR ended up bigger than intended because covering those reliably took more work.

I won't promise a full cleanup in the next few days, but I will push the specific refactors you suggested: reduce the inline if ($isPostgres) branches where possible, centralize more of the dialect-specific building (following @shinde-rahul's idea of a clearer abstraction point), and clean up the duplicated methods.

All scattered platform checks and all shared code handling the differences between the PostgreSQL and MySQL dialects will be implemented in the DatabasePlatform class (single place to review), which looks like the best place for this purpose. This will eliminate the need for scattered If(platform) checks throughout the core code.

These reviews were actually expected and were exactly the reason this PR was being a draft. To get the working code reviewed early and gather feedback on the approach. The code itself works, but the current implementation is not yet at the production standard. That's why I wanted reviews before finalizing the architecture.

On maintenance: as mentioned before, I will personally handle PostgreSQL-related fixes going forward. I'm already running this fork in production (sending ~10 million emails/month), so any conflict, bug, or incompatibility that surfaces gets fixed on my side. No extra burden on the core team.

So the current plan is to:
- Short term (coming weeks): address the review comments, reduce scattering, improve query handling for the mentioned differences.
- After that: keep the PR focused on compatibility without major refactoring.
- Ongoing: I maintain Postgres fixes; core stays MySQL-first.

@escopecz Update (following @shinde-rahul's idea of a clearer abstraction point):

Consolidated platform-specific logic into the central **Mautic\CoreBundle\Doctrine\DatabasePlatform** class.
Remaining **DatabasePlatform::isPostgreSQL()** checks and why they stay:
1. **app/bundles/InstallBundle/EventListener/DoctrineEventSubscriber.php** → **postgreSqlMySqlCompact()** method - runs only on PostgreSQL during schema generation to create MySQL compatibility functions/operators (e.g. **date_format**, **convert_tz**, **ifnull**, boolean/integer operators). This is intentional and required for fresh installs.
2. **app/bundles/InstallBundle/Helper/SchemaHelper.php** → **installSchema()**, **backupExistingSchema()**, **dropExistingSchema()** - handles PostgreSQL-specific differences during installation like dropping sequences, backing up/renaming sequences, skipping **foreign_key_checks** (which does not exist on PostgreSQL) etc. These paths are required for the installer to work correctly on both platforms.
3. **app/bundles/CoreBundle/Test/MauticMysqlTestCase.php** - several methods use platform checks for transaction/rollback behavior, sequence handling, psql vs mysql commands, and dump/reset SQL generation etc. These are test infrastructure and deliberately platform-aware.
4. Tests:
* app/bundles/LeadBundle/Tests/EventListener/CampaignSubscriberFunctionalTest.php (testRegexOperatorOnDateFieldCondition) - keeps $useCleanupRollback disabled only for MySQL (to avoid "There is no active transaction" exception occur on MySQL - original test creator intention).
* app/bundles/CoreBundle/Tests/Functional/EventListener/MigrationCommandSubscriberTest.php - generated columns assertions on PostgreSQL (they are not immutable in the same way, so the test is marked as partly skipped).
5. 7 legacy migration files - old migrations (not executed on new installs) but must still run successfully when importing/upgrading from very old databases. They contain checks for:
* **foreign_key_checks** (MySQL-only)
* table field types
* charset/collation handling (PostgreSQL uses different syntax/behavior here)

Everywhere else in the codebase, scattered inline **isPostgreSQL()** checks have been removed and replaced with calls to the centralized **DatabasePlatform** helpers.

The remaining checks are isolated to:
* installation schema preparation
* legacy migration compatibility
* test-specific edge cases

We've been running this branch (`7.x-postgresql`) against PostgreSQL 16 and hit a reproducible failure on every `doctrine:migrations:migrate` run:

```
SQLSTATE[42P16]: multiple primary keys for table "migrations" are not allowed
```

**Root cause**: `app/config/config.php` applies `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true` to the connection options unconditionally (it's there as a MySQL/PHP 8.1 workaround). On `pdo_pgsql`, the option also stringifies the booleans returned by DBAL's schema-introspection queries against `pg_catalog` (e.g. `pg_index.indisprimary`/`indisunique`), which breaks DBAL's boolean handling — `introspectTable()` ends up reporting **zero indexes** for every table. doctrine-migrations then thinks the `migrations` table has no primary key and emits `ALTER TABLE migrations ADD PRIMARY KEY (version)` on every run → 42P16.

**Fix that works for us** — make the option conditional on the driver:

```php
'options' => 'pdo_pgsql' === $localConfigParameterBag->get('db_driver')
    ? []
    : [PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true],
```

With that change, introspection is correct and `mautic:install` + all migrations run cleanly on PostgreSQL; we have the branch passing our end-to-end suite (install → login → dashboard) with it.

> ```
> ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES
> ```

Hi @thib-d . Thanks for the detailed report and the suggested fix.

I've already removed the unconditional `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES` (no longer needed with PHP 8.2+ / MySQL 8.4+). 

Appreciate the help.

Thanks @adiati98 — Promptless is reviewing the Dynamic Web Content documentation updates in this pull request against the source change and the Mautic docs style guide. We'll follow up here with suggested edits, or a note if the changes already look good.

Thanks @adiati98 — I inspected the code PR (mautic/mautic#15038, "Enable Dynamic Web Content in Email builder") and reviewed against it, the Copilot comments, and our style guide. Summary below; suggested edits are inline.

**Your comments**

**1. Back-to-back admonitions (the three notes after the Email-token steps).** Agreed — folded into a single note with an unordered list:

````suggestion
.. note::

   * Only Dynamic Web Content items with the Text type are available as Email tokens. You can't use HTML items in Emails.
   * Mautic only evaluates published Dynamic Web Content items. It skips unpublished items even if their filters would match the Contact.
   * Mautic tracks Dynamic Web Content token usage and makes it available in the Dynamic Web Content Report.
````

**2. Hyphen instead of parentheses** (API intro line, currently `...authentication headers (see :doc:...).`):

````suggestion
You can manage Dynamic Web Content display order programmatically via the Mautic API. Replace ``example.com`` with your Mautic instance domain and include the required authentication headers - see :doc:`/authentication/authentication`. To update the slot name and display order of a Dynamic Web Content item:
````

**Copilot comments**

- **Terminology + UI label on the Order/Priority field** (Copilot, line ~90): fixed the term and formatted the option per our style guide (interactive options are **bold**, not quoted). Note the option's real label is **Put at Beginning** (capital B), and Mautic evaluates in *ascending* order (lowest first):

````suggestion
- **Order/Priority** - shown if using non-Campaign based Dynamic Web Content, this allows you to specify the display order when multiple Dynamic Web Content items share the same slot name. Select an order to place your new Dynamic Web Content item right after it in the list. To set it as the first item, choose **Put at Beginning**. Mautic evaluates the filters of Dynamic Web Content items in ascending order - lowest first - until it finds a match.
````
  (Heads-up: Vale's `Vale.Terms` rule will flag *Put* → *PUT* on this line. It's a false positive — this is the UI button label, not the HTTP verb — so it can be dismissed, or wrapped in a narrow `.. vale off` / `.. vale on` if you'd prefer CI green.)

- **DWC email token syntax** (Copilot: "should be `{dwc=slotName}` with no closing tag / no default content"): this one I'd **dismiss** — the PR is correct as written. In #15038 the Email builder inserts the paired form `{dwc=slot-name}Default content goes here{/dwc}` (`DwcTokensSubscriber::DWCTOKENREGEX`) and Mautic validates that the default content is present (`DwcTokenValidator`, wired to the Email subject in `Email.php`); a bare `{dwc=slot}` or empty `{dwc=slot}{/dwc}` triggers the *"...default content missing between opening and closing tags"* error. When no filter matches, the embedded default content is shown. So the documented paired syntax and the "default content is mandatory" note are accurate.

- **API base URL / auth** (Copilot, line ~292): already addressed in the latest revision — the example now uses `https://example.com/api/...` and points to the authentication docs. ✅

**Mautic terms & accuracy (from the source)**

- **Reports section** — the column list has two items the report doesn't actually expose. `sent count` and a `Filter` column aren't in the DWC report definition (`DynamicContentReportSubscriber`); the real columns include Name, Slot Name, Order/Priority, Date Sent, a Target Location (Subject Line/Body), plus Contact and Category columns. Suggested correction:

````suggestion
   * Dynamic Web Content name, Slot Name, and Order/Priority
   * Date Sent and Target Location - Subject Line or Body
   * Contact information for tracking individual interactions
   * Category information
````

- **Variations tab** (line ~113–115): the tab lists *all* items sharing the slot (including the current one, marked as current) and only appears when more than one item shares the slot name. Also worth noting the tab sorts *descending* while filter evaluation is *ascending*, so consider softening "helping you understand the priority in which Mautic evaluates filters" to avoid implying the displayed order is the evaluation order.

- **Minor Vale/terms**: `content type set to **Text**` → `type set to **Text**` (avoids the `content type` → `media type` warning and matches the field); the `Adding tokens to Emails` heading keeps *Emails* capitalized per our Mautic-terms rule (that Google.Headings sentence-case warning is a deliberate exception).

**Not introduced by this PR (optional):** Copilot's "vale toggle breaks the list" note on the *Creating slots* value list is pre-existing — that list already mixes `-`/`#.` bullets and `.. vale off` interruptions in the base file, so it's out of scope here unless you'd like it cleaned up separately.

**Branch targeting (heads-up):** this PR is based on the **7.1** docs branch, but since the source change (#15038) targets Mautic 7.x, the update may belong on the **7.3** docs branch instead. Flagging it in case you'd prefer it land there — your call.

rawCodeReviews.body: Works as expected 👍
Okay then
All set from my side.

I validated this locally,

### What I checked

1. Created a `Visits specific URL` point action in the UI.
2. Set:
   - Page URL: `https://example.com/pricing`
   - Total time spent: `60 seconds`
   - Returns after: `1 hour`
3. Saved the action successfully.
4. Confirmed the stored properties include:
   - `accumulative_time = 60`
   - `returns_after = 3600`

### Reproduction case

1. Contact has a previous hit for `https://example.com/pricing`.
2. That hit has `date_left` set so the dwell time is 90 seconds.
3. Only 10 minutes have passed.
4. The contact now visits `https://example.com/blog`.

### Actual result

`validateUrlHit()` returns `true`.

### Expected result

It should return `false`, because `returns_after = 3600` is configured but the current hit is not for `/pricing`, and only 10 minutes have passed.

The issue seems to be that `accumulative_time` is added to `$changePoints` from historical data, but `returns_after` is only added inside the `$urlMatches` block. When `$urlMatches` is false, the configured `returns_after` condition disappears from the final evaluation.

rawDocsReviews.body: @promptless-for-oss some changes needed here. I am not sure if you can fix some of them.

rawDocsComments.body: Thanks for the detailed review @RCheesley — going through each comment now. I'll re-capture and re-annotate the flagged screenshots (the red box on **Change Segments**, the red arrow on the bottom connector, the correct top item reading **Delete contacts in this segment**, and the images marked as looking off), and I'll follow up here with the results, including a clear note on anything that can't be reproduced in our capture environment.

Diagnosed each flagged image against the originals. The main issue is that the new batch was captured at half the resolution of the original 2x screenshots, so several look blurry; a couple also caught the wrong viewport or state. Two show the wrong content — the connector image and the top source node reading **Visited Product A** instead of **Delete contacts in this segment** — and two need the red-box/arrow annotations restored (**Change Segments** and the bottom connector). All ten are reproducible in our capture environment. Bringing up a local Mautic 5.2 instance to re-capture and re-annotate everything at 2x now.

Thanks for the detailed review @RCheesley — all ten items are addressed and pushed (HEAD `5535ac9`):

- The blurry "what happened here?" images were captured at 1x by mistake; they've been recaptured at 2x. The create-segment shot no longer clips the right column, and the date filter now shows a clean calendar without the stray time-picker overlay.
- The red box is back around **Change Segments**.
- A red arrow now points at the campaign source node's bottom connector.
- A red box now marks **Preferences**.
- The bulk-delete canvas was recaptured so the top source node correctly reads 'Delete contacts in this segment' instead of 'Visited Product A'.

All ten were reproducible in the capture environment — none had to be skipped. No prose changed. Ready for another look.

Thanks @RCheesley — working through each comment. I'll fix the **SMAL** → **SAML** filename typo, and re-capture the screenshots where settings sections came out empty (including checking the PHP IMAP extension in the capture environment). I'll follow up here with the results and a clear note on anything that can't be reproduced in our capture environment.

Mapped all the flagged images to their causes. Most of the "settings missing" shots are the message-queue and email DSN builders captured with the fields left empty, so they show blank example values — re-capturing those with example DSNs filled in to match the previously published images. Your hypothesis on the monitored-inbox screenshot is correct: the PHP IMAP extension wasn't loaded, so Mautic hid the form and showed the 'IMAP extension is required' banner — I'm working on getting IMAP available in the capture environment so that section renders. I'll also fix the **SMAL** → **SAML** filename typo. Will follow up with the results.

I noticed that some CI checks failed for this PR. I'm investigating whether the failures are caused by this suggestion. If they're unrelated or pre-existing, I'll leave this suggestion unchanged and create a separate suggestion if a standalone docs fix is needed.

Thanks @RCheesley — all your comments are addressed (commit `17ac15e`):

- **Message queue + Email DSN screenshots** (sync, Doctrine, Redis, AMQP, Beanstalkd, Amazon SQS, the failure queue, plus SMTP and SendGrid) were previously captured on a fresh install before any DSN was entered, so the fields showed empty. They've been recaptured with the documented example DSN values filled in.
- **Filename typo** fixed: `SMAL-settings.png` → `SAML-settings.png`, with its image directive updated.
- **Monitored Inbox** — you were exactly right: that section only showed the 'PHP IMAP extension is required' banner because IMAP wasn't loaded in the capture environment. Our screenshot toolchain runs on PHP 8.4, which dropped IMAP from core with no installable package, so that form can't be rendered there. We've restored the previously published screenshot that shows the full form; a fresh 5.2 capture of just that section would need a capture environment with the PHP IMAP extension available.

Separately, heads-up: the failing **build** check isn't caused by these image changes — it's a pre-existing broken external link (`https://aivie.ch`, returning HTTP 415) in `docs/builders/email_landing_page.rst`, which is outside this PR's scope and identical on the base branch. Ready for another look.

rawDocsReviews.body: @promptless-for-oss some attention needed in this PR, too.

rawDocsComments.body: Thanks @RCheesley — on it. I'll re-capture the multi-source campaign image with more horizontal space so the connection between the two sources is visible, and inspect the other flagged images to fix whatever went wrong. I'll follow up here with the results, including a note on anything that can't be reproduced in our capture environment.

Diagnosed the three flagged images: the multi-source campaign shot has the two source boxes butted together so the connector between them is hidden; the paste-cloned-event modal is clipped so its frame reads as broken; and the send-email delay-options shot is cut off on the right with the selected tabs rendering solid black. All three are framing/capture-state issues. Re-capturing them against a local Mautic 5.2 instance at 2x now — no prose changes.

Thanks for the review @RCheesley — all three flagged Campaign Builder screenshots have been recaptured against a fresh Mautic 5.2 instance and pushed (commit `c8f9139`):

- **`multi-source-campaign.png`** ("add more horizontal space between the two sources") → recaptured with the two Contact source boxes dragged apart so the connector between them is clearly visible.
- **`send-email-delay-options.png`** ("what happened here?") → the previous image was cropped on the right, cutting off the last delay tab; recaptured at full width so the whole "Execute this event…" tab row (immediately / at a relative time period / at a specific date/time / optimal for contact) is visible.
- **`paste-cloned-event-modal.png`** ("what happened here?") → the previous image was clipped at the top so the modal looked broken; recaptured with the complete modal frame intact.

The other three images and all prose are unchanged. One transparency note: our sandbox browser wouldn't honor a retina/device-scale override, so these three were captured at 1x and upscaled to 2x to match the repo's image sizing — the text is sharp and all the framing/state issues are fixed, but if you specifically want native-2x pixel density, that would need a capture environment where we can set the device scale factor. Happy to pursue that if you'd like. Ready for another look.

Thanks @RCheesley — I'll restore the red box around the user permissions link and the one around the Identity provider metadata file box, matching the original screenshots, and follow up here once done.

Both review comments are addressed on this PR (commit `01a74a7`):

- **User Permissions link** (`roles-permissions.png`) — red box restored around the **User Permissions (0 / 12)** list item.
- **Identity provider metadata file** (`turn-on-saml.png`) — red box restored around the **Identity provider metadata file** label and its Choose File input.

Since you'd accepted the fresh Mautic 5.2 captures themselves, we re-annotated the existing images to match the original red-box style rather than recapturing. No prose or image directives changed, and the third image (`authentication-settings.png`) was left unchanged as it drew no comment. Ready for another look.
Thanks @RCheesley — I'll change the annotation on the Integrations menu screenshot so the **Plugins** item has a red box instead of a red underline, and follow up here once done.

Thanks @RCheesley — done (commit `c928864`). The **Plugins** menu item on the Integrations admin menu screenshot (`docs/plugins/images/plugins.png`) now has a red box around it instead of the red underline, matching the highlight style used on the other 5.2 image updates. The underlying Mautic 5.2.0 screenshot is unchanged, and the other two images in the PR are untouched. Ready for another look.

rawDocsComments.body: Thanks @RCheesley — looking into the images that didn't come through correctly. I'll inspect each flagged screenshot, figure out what went wrong, and re-capture or re-upload them, then follow up here with the results (including a note on anything that can't be reproduced in our capture environment).

Diagnosed the five flagged images — each was captured or cropped incorrectly in the prior run. The trigger-events list image was reduced to a narrow strip with all page context lost; the New Point Trigger and New Point Action forms are clipped at the top, missing their headers and the Save/Cancel button bar; and the two "Send an email" trigger modals were captured without the page backdrop and with the footer clipped. Re-capturing all five against a live Mautic 6.0.9 instance at 2x with correct full framing. The other four (unflagged) images look fine and stay as-is. Will follow up with the results.

Thanks for flagging these @RCheesley — you were right that several images hadn't uploaded correctly. Five screenshots had been cropped incorrectly in the first upload (commit `a90c528` fixes all of them):

- **`trigger-events.png`** was reduced to a bare strip of the 'Add an event' dropdown.
- **`points-action.png`** and **`points-trigger.png`** were clipped at the top, losing the page header and the Save / Save & Close / Cancel bar.
- The two **Send an email** modal shots (`point_trigger_send_an_email.png`, `point_trigger_send_an_email_to_user.png`) lost their backdrop and had the Add / Cancel footer cut off.

All five have been recaptured against a live Mautic 6.0.9 instance in light mode at 2x with the correct full framing. The four non-flagged modal images are unchanged. One thing worth noting: in 6.0.9 the 'Send an email' modal is now nested under a 'Trigger Action Details' heading — that's a genuine 6.0 UI change, not a capture glitch, so it's reflected in the new screenshots. Ready for another look.

rawDocsReviews.body: Small suggestion - the theme used in the original is called Brienz.

rawDocsComments.body: Thanks @RCheesley — good call. I'll recapture the Email Builder overview using the **Brienz** theme (as in the original) instead of the blank theme, redraw the five numbered callouts, and follow up here once done.

Confirmed — the current image is the blank "Hello World" theme, while the original used the richer Brienz newsletter template. Standing up a local Mautic 6.0.9 instance to recapture the Email Builder overview with the Brienz theme, then redrawing the five numbered callouts (device-size toggles, undo/redo, editor toolbar, Sections panel, Blocks panel) to match the prose.

Thanks @RCheesley — good catch. I've recaptured the Email Builder overview using the **Brienz** theme so it matches the original instead of the blank/default theme. The builder canvas now shows the richer Brienz newsletter (logo, hero image, headline, and the "MORE UPDATES" button), and the five numbered callouts have been redrawn to line up with the numbered list in the prose. Captured on a local Mautic 6.0.9 instance at 2x, pushed as SHA `43fd136`. Could you take another look when you have a moment?

Thanks @RCheesley — I'll inspect the two flagged Campaign Builder images, figure out what went wrong, and re-capture them, then follow up here with the results (including a note on anything that can't be reproduced in our capture environment).

Diagnosed the two flagged images — both are clipped captures. The paste-cloned-event modal lost its top event node and connector and is cut off at the edges, and the send-email delay-options shot has the heading clipped at the top with a broken overlapping footer at the bottom. Re-capturing both correctly against a local Mautic 6.0.x instance at 2x, matching the framing of the four accepted images in this PR. Will follow up with the results.

Thanks for flagging those two images @RCheesley — both were botched in the previous capture (commit `9fb5feb` fixes them):

- **`send-email-delay-options.png`** — the heading was cut off and a dark Add/Cancel bar was overlapping the Priority/Attempts fields. Recaptured to show the full modal top-to-bottom with a clean footer.
- **`paste-cloned-event-modal.png`** — the Decision/Action/Condition cards were clipped at both edges. Recaptured with all three cards fully in-frame plus the 'Insert cloned event here' panel.

Both were recaptured against a fresh Mautic 6.0.9 instance at 2x and now match the framing of the other images in the PR. The other four images are unchanged. Ready for another look.
Thanks @RCheesley — I'll change the annotation on the Integrations menu screenshot so the **Plugins** item has a red box instead of a red underline, and follow up here once done.

Thanks @RCheesley — done (commit `f611146`). The **Plugins** menu item on the Integrations admin menu screenshot (`docs/plugins/images/plugins.png`) is now marked with a red square box instead of the red underline, matching the annotation style used across the other Plugin resources image updates (including the 5.2 sibling). This reuses the existing Mautic 7.0.2 capture — annotation-only, no recapture. Ready for another look.

Thanks for putting this together! I reviewed the content against the implementation and it's accurate: the location (**Contact Behavior and Actions**), the filter label, and all six operators match the behaviour of the underlying `ForeignValueFilterQueryBuilder`.

One small wording suggestion, since these two operators are easy to mix up:

- **excluding any of** — contacts who submitted *none* of the selected Forms.
- **excluding all of** — contacts who did *not* submit the *complete set* of selected Forms (i.e. they're missing at least one; someone who submitted some but not all is still included).

The current text for *excluding all of* ("haven't submitted all of the selected Forms") is technically correct, this just adds the contrast for readers. Everything else looks good to me. ✨

Thanks for the careful review, @introfini! Updated the two "excluding" bullets to spell out the contrast:

- **excluding any of** — Contacts who submitted *none* of the selected Forms.
- **excluding all of** — Contacts who haven't submitted the complete set of selected Forms (they're missing at least one, so someone who submitted some but not all is still included).

All other operator descriptions, the steps, and the tip are unchanged, since you confirmed those match the `ForeignValueFilterQueryBuilder` behaviour. Pushed to the PR branch. 🙏

rawCodeReviews.body:
Code looks good. It works.

Maybe ... consider cache usage because of using COUNT() on big segments could be slow.
Can be added later in next PR.

TY!

Could you load these statistics asynchronously, similar to how you handle contact statistics with `contactStatsAction()` and `getStatsSummaryForContacts()`? Right now, these calls perform two full segment membership scans on every initial page load, including the filter-added count even when its card isn't displayed. This could become a performance issue on larger systems.

The new endpoint could return the total, manually added, and filter-added counts in a single aggregate query. You could then cache that result if segment membership changes can reliably invalidate it. Async loading or caching alone would still perform both scans on every cache miss.

Promptless prepared documentation updates related to this change.

Triggered by [PR #16228](https://github.com/mautic/mautic/pull/16228) in mautic/mautic

**User Documentation:**
Documents the new Filters tab in Focus Items that allows automatic display to Contacts matching filter criteria via the Mautic tracking script. Reorganizes the deployment section to present three clear methods: filter-based delivery, direct embedding, and Campaign delivery.

Review: [Document Contact filters for Focus Items](https://github.com/mautic/user-documentation/pull/756)

**Developer Documentation:**
Adds documentation for `MauticJS.setTrackedContact()` and `MauticJS.beforeFirstEventDelivery()` API functions that enable loading contact-specific content via the tracking script.

Review: [Document MauticJS tracking API functions for contact-specific content](https://github.com/mautic/developer-documentation-new/pull/521)

## Pull request overview This PR adds Dynamic Web Content–style contact filters to Focus items so that eligible published Focus items can be automatically injected on tracked visits via `mtc.js`, without requiring manual embeds or campaigns. **Changes:** - Adds a nullable `filters` column to `focus` (via migration) and exposes it via serializer groups for Focus API read/write. - Extends the Focus edit UI with a new Filters tab using the existing DWC filters entry type/theme and shared filter JS initialization. - Implements automatic delivery: `mtc.js` conditionally calls a new public `/focus/check` endpoint which returns matching Focus item JS URLs for the tracked contact, with functional tests covering key scenarios. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 17 out of 17 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.

@promptless-for-oss can you make a docs PR for this one please. We need one PR for user docs and one PR for the developer docs.

I was quite excited about the [proposal](https://community.mautic.org/processes/roadmap/f/4/proposals/200) as it was suggesting to bend Postgres with polyfills to support Mautic rather than bending Mautic to support Postgres. However, in this PR I can see major Mautic refactoring. Lots of ifs where one query is used for MySql and MariaDB and completely different query is used for Postgres. When you look at the size of this PR it's clear how massive change it is. It'll take weeks just to review this. I'm pretty sure there are tens of bugs hidden in this PR. So we'll need good user base that require Mautic running on Postgres that will help us review and test this PR. Because if it is still just 1% then such a massive change that makes the code even harder to maintain isn't worth it. This is why we've decided to drop support for Posgres in the first place.

I've considered a better database abstraction layer for Mautic for some time. Inserting another abstraction layer for all data-driven interactions is very appealing. Such a mechanism would allow us to use different backend data sources  depending on what's being requested. Have some documents in MongoDB? Go get them through the data layer Mongo datasource. Need to operate on your campaigns from Salesforce? Get them through the data layer's Salesforce datasource. This would prevent us from having to manage the seemingly neverending data sync issues that come hand-in-hand with our current integrations. 

There's plenty of architectural benefits of this approach. By managing the data layer in this way, we could intercept and act on any request for data, modifying or otherwise combining various data sources into a normalized structure. We could take a request like `$this->datalayer->contacts->all()` and pull in local db contacts, remote contacts from an API response, and query the filesystem of an old ERP. We could more easily implement an [event sourcing](https://eventsauce.io/) approach which comes with all sorts of benefits on its own (data rollbacks, replays, insight into what happened for audit purposes). 

That said, such a system could be rather impractical both to implement and in real world usage without major changes that go beyond the scope of what even this PR is trying to accomplish. I'm not opposed to supporting pgsql, but I would like to see it implemented in a particular way if we really want it. I'm open to discussion.

Thanks for the detailed reviews, @escopecz @shinde-rahul @dongilbert. You're right to call out the scattered DB-specific logic and the growth in scope.

The original plan was a small, contained change like the POC: mostly platform tweaks, quoting fixes, and minimal adjustments to keep everything working on both MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL without breaking existing installs. Doctrine 2.x limits cleaner abstraction options, so some conditionals and duplicated query parts crept in as we hit real edge cases in tests and production data. Things like LIKE vs ILIKE (with LOWER), REGEXP differences, date formatting (DATE_FORMAT vs TO_CHAR), GROUP BY strictness, and upsert behavior all needed handling. The PR ended up bigger than intended because covering those reliably took more work.

I won't promise a full cleanup in the next few days, but I will push the specific refactors you suggested: reduce the inline if ($isPostgres) branches where possible, centralize more of the dialect-specific building (following @shinde-rahul's idea of a clearer abstraction point), and clean up the duplicated methods.

All scattered platform checks and all shared code handling the differences between the PostgreSQL and MySQL dialects will be implemented in the DatabasePlatform class (single place to review), which looks like the best place for this purpose. This will eliminate the need for scattered If(platform) checks throughout the core code.

These reviews were actually expected and were exactly the reason this PR was being a draft. To get the working code reviewed early and gather feedback on the approach. The code itself works, but the current implementation is not yet at the production standard. That's why I wanted reviews before finalizing the architecture.

On maintenance: as mentioned before, I will personally handle PostgreSQL-related fixes going forward. I'm already running this fork in production (sending ~10 million emails/month), so any conflict, bug, or incompatibility that surfaces gets fixed on my side. No extra burden on the core team.

- Short term (coming weeks): address the review comments, reduce scattering, improve query handling for the mentioned differences.

- Ongoing: I maintain Postgres fixes; core stays MySQL-first.

2. **app/bundles/InstallBundle/Helper/SchemaHelper.php** → **installSchema()**, **backupExistingSchema()**, **dropExistingSchema()** - handles PostgreSQL-specific differences during installation like dropping sequences, backing up/renaming sequences, skipping **foreign_key_checks** (which does not exist on PostgreSQL) etc. These paths are required for the installer to work correctly on both platforms.
3. **app/bundles/CoreBundle/Test/MauticMysqlTestCase.php** - several methods use platform checks for transaction/rollback behavior, sequence handling, psql vs mysql commands, and dump/reset SQL generation etc. These are test infrastructure and deliberately platform-aware.
4. Tests:
* app/bundles/LeadBundle/Tests/EventListener/CampaignSubscriberFunctionalTest.php (testRegexOperatorOnDateFieldCondition) - keeps $useCleanupRollback disabled only for MySQL (to avoid "There is no active transaction" exception occur on MySQL - original test creator intention).
* app/bundles/CoreBundle/Tests/Functional/EventListener/MigrationCommandSubscriberTest.php - generated columns assertions on PostgreSQL (they are not immutable in the same way, so the test is marked as partly skipped).
5. 7 legacy migration files - old migrations (not executed on new installs) but must still run successfully when importing/upgrading from very old databases. They contain checks for:
* **foreign_key_checks** (MySQL-only)
* table field types
* charset/collation handling (PostgreSQL uses different syntax/behavior here)

Everywhere else in the codebase, scattered inline **isPostgreSQL()** checks have been removed and replaced with calls to the centralized **DatabasePlatform** helpers.

The remaining checks are isolated to:
* installation schema preparation
* legacy migration compatibility
* test-specific edge cases

We've been running this branch (`7.x-postgresql`) against PostgreSQL 16 and hit a reproducible failure on every `doctrine:migrations:migrate` run:

```
SQLSTATE[42P16]: multiple primary keys for table "migrations" are not allowed
```

**Root cause**: `app/config/config.php` applies `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true` to the connection options unconditionally (it's there as a MySQL/PHP 8.1 workaround). On `pdo_pgsql`, the option also stringifies the booleans returned by DBAL's schema-introspection queries against `pg_catalog` (e.g. `pg_index.indisprimary`/`indisunique`), which breaks DBAL's boolean handling — `introspectTable()` ends up reporting **zero indexes** for every table. doctrine-migrations then thinks the `migrations` table has no primary key and emits `ALTER TABLE migrations ADD PRIMARY KEY (version)` on every run → 42P16.

**Fix that works for us** — make the option conditional on the driver:

```php
'options' => 'pdo_pgsql' === $localConfigParameterBag->get('db_driver')
    ? []
    : [PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES => true],
```

With that change, introspection is correct and `mautic:install` + all migrations run cleanly on PostgreSQL; we have the branch passing our end-to-end suite (install → login → dashboard) with it.

> ```
> ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES
> ```

Hi @thib-d . Thanks for the detailed report and the suggested fix.

I've already removed the unconditional `PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES` (no longer needed with PHP 8.2+ / MySQL 8.4+). 

Appreciate the help.

Reintroduces PostgreSQL support across Mautic 7.x by adding a compatibility layer for DBAL/SQL differences (quoting, LIKE/ILIKE/regex, migrations, installer/config), while keeping MySQL/MariaDB behavior consistent.

- Normalizes query behavior across DBs (identifier quoting, LIKE/ILIKE, regex, DISTINCT semantics, interval/time functions).
- Updates functional/unit tests and installer/config to run deterministically on PostgreSQL as well as MySQL/MariaDB.

Some key things to consider:

Please use VSCode with the extensions, it should automatically lint for you and tell you the issues as you type.  The main things are using brackets - use hyphens instead - and the links. 

Please use RST linking to link to other sections/pages. Every title is unique so you can just the ref: role to link to them enclosed in backticks. Always try to link to the appropriate sub-section of the page using the relevant heading rather than just linking to the page, it's more useful for the reader.
